prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one universal “best” roofer — the best choice depends on your location in Denver, your roof type, your insurance claim situation, and which contractor is available and reputable at the time. I can help you find a top option for your address, or show you how to pick the best local hail‑damage roofer.

How to find the best Denver roofer for hail damage
- Use manufacturer locators: look up GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed contractor locators for certified installers (Master Elite, Certified, etc.).
- Check reviews and ratings: Google Maps, Yelp, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), and the Better Business Bureau for recent reviews and complaints.
- Ask your insurer for preferred/approved contractors, but still vet them independently.
- Contact the Colorado Roofing Association or local trade groups for referrals.

Must‑check criteria (quick checklist)
- Local physical office and local references (recent hail repairs nearby).
- Valid insurance (liability and workers’ comp) and bonding; ask to see certificates.
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) for better warranties.
- Experience with insurance claims and Xactimate (so estimates align with adjusters).
- Written, itemized estimate and scope of work (materials, underlayment, flashing, ventilation).
- Clear warranty terms: workmanship and manufacturer shingle warranty.
- Permits and inspections included in scope.
- Payment terms: avoid paying large upfront sums; get lien waivers on progress payments.
- Written final inspection and clean‑up clause (all nails removed).

Red flags / things to avoid
- Door‑to‑door “storm chasers” with no local office or license.
- High-pressure sales, “limited storm special” push to sign immediately.
- Only take cash or insist on full payment up front.
- No written contract or vague scope.

Questions to ask any roofer
- How long have you been repairing hail damage in Denver? Can I see recent local references/photos?
- Are you licensed/insured in Colorado? Can you provide certificates?
- Are you a certified installer with any shingle manufacturers?
- Do you handle permits and coordinate with my insurance adjuster?
- What is the warranty on workmanship and materials? Is it transferable?
- What is the full breakdown of costs and timeline?
- Do you provide a final invoice and lien waivers?

If you want a quick shortlist of reputable contractors in your area, tell me your Denver zip code and whether you prefer national firms or local companies. I can then help you compare 3–5 options and draft questions or an email to send to them.
